    AI Overview
    UCLA
     holds the record for the most NCAA Division I men's basketball national championships, with 11 titles. The Bruins famously won 10 of these championships under head coach John Wooden between 1964 and 1975, including seven consecutive titles from 1967 to 1973. 
    Top NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Champions: 
    • UCLA: 11 (1964, 1965, 1967, 1968, 1969, 1970, 1971, 1972, 1973, 1975, 1995)
    • Kentucky: 8 (1948, 1949, 1951, 1958, 1978, 1996, 1998, 2012)
    • North Carolina: 6 (1957, 1982, 1993, 2005, 2009, 2017)
    • UConn: 6 (1999, 2004, 2011, 2014, 2023, 2024)
    • Duke: 5 (1991, 1992, 2001, 2010, 2015)
    • Indiana: 5 (1940, 1953, 1976, 1981, 1987) 
    UCLA's 1995 title was the only one won outside of the John Wooden era.

    UCLA
     holds the record for the most NCAA Division I men’s basketball championships with 11 titles. Under coach John Wooden, the Bruins dominated by winning 10 titles in 12 seasons (1964–1975) and added an 11th in 1995. 
    Top 5 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Champions: 
    • UCLA: 11 (1964, 1965, 1967, 1968, 1969, 1970, 1971, 1972, 1973, 1975, 1995)
    • Kentucky: 8 (1948, 1949, 1951, 1958, 1978, 1996, 1998, 2012)
    • North Carolina: 6 (1957, 1982, 1993, 2005, 2009, 2017)
    • UConn: 6 (1999, 2004, 2011, 2014, 2023, 2024)
    • Duke:
      5 (1991, 1992, 2001, 2010, 2015)
    • Indiana: 5 (1940, 1953, 1976, 1981, 1987) 
    UCLA also holds the record for the most consecutive championships, winning seven straight from 1967 to 1973.
